title: Perf benchmarking sync notes — 2026-07-14
content:
Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Samir Patel, Lina Gomez, Elliot Park, Maya Singh, QA: Jordan Li, SRE: Priya Nair

Agenda:
- Quick status and high-level summary of latest nightlies
- Investigate reported latency regressions (p99) for long-sequence workloads
- Review throughput anomalies on H100 pools after kernel-selection change
- Action items and next steps / who runs follow-ups

Summary of findings (TL;DR):
- We observed a p99 latency regression (~1.6x) for long-sequence (seq_len >= 2048) generation workloads on redwood-v1-large yesterday after deploying the kernel-selection optimizer (PR #2481).
- Throughput for short-sequence (seq_len <= 512) workloads was largely unaffected; in some cases it improved marginally (~5-8%) on A100.
- H100 dedicated pools saw intermittent throughput drops in the 10-20% range for batched sampling workloads (batch size 8-16) when using the new kv-cache merge path.
- Reverting the kernel-selection flag for a subset of instances made p99 latencies return to baseline; this isolates the root cause to kernel selection + long sequence path interaction.

Key data from nightly runs (2026-07-13 02:00 → 2026-07-14 02:00):
- Test harness: infra/benchmarks/harness-v5 (Jenkins job: bench/nightly-serving-runtime-07-13)
- Workloads tested: sampling (top-p), greedy, chat-streaming, embeddings (batch 64)

Representative numbers (median / p99):
- redwood-v1-large (A100, bf16)
  - seq_len 256, batch 8: throughput 1920 tok/s median, p99 latency 72 ms (baseline ~70 ms)
  - seq_len 1024, batch 8: throughput 740 tok/s median, p99 latency 210 ms (baseline ~205 ms)
  - seq_len 2048, batch 8: throughput 360 tok/s median, p99 latency 590 ms (regressed from baseline 370 ms)

- redwood-v1-large (H100, bf16, kernel-select enabled)
  - seq_len 512, batch 8: throughput 1350 tok/s median, p99 latency 95 ms (improved vs baseline 102 ms)
  - seq_len 2048, batch 8: throughput 320 tok/s median, p99 latency 610 ms (regressed from baseline 360 ms)

- quantized-redwood-v1-large (4-bit, A100)
  - seq_len 512, batch 16: throughput 1600 tok/s median, p99 latency 120 ms (baseline 115 ms)
  - seq_len 2048, batch 16: throughput 280 tok/s median, p99 latency 780 ms (regressed, baseline 390 ms)

Notes on measurements and confidence:
- All runs executed with stable client harness and identical prompt sets (cached prefixes disabled unless otherwise noted).
- Regression is consistent across multiple runs and reproduces locally on a dev H100 node when kernel-select is active.
- p50 and median throughputs show much smaller variance; the main impact is p99/jitter due to a fallback path that activates for long KV-cache management with the new kernel selection heuristics.

Investigation details:
- Root cause hypothesis: the new kernel-selection optimizer (PR #2481) picks a kernel path that reduces aggregate arithmetic ops for common shapes but triggers a suboptimal memory copy / kv-merge sequence for >1024 token contexts. This path interacts poorly with the streaming-kv eviction logic and causes occasional stalls while merging large KV segments.
- Reproduction steps used:
  1) Checkout serving-runtime@pr-2481 branch locally
  2) Run bench/harness-v5 with PROFILE_KSELECT=1 and a prepared long-seq prompt set
  3) Observe p99 spikes in logs and correlate with stack traces captured by the perf probe
- Logs / traces: stack traces show repeated memcpy calls and blocking on cudaMemcpyAsync followed by a small number of kernel launches confirming the stall pattern.

Mitigation & fixes considered:
- Short-term rollback: disable kernel-selection optimizer in the staging cluster (flag: runtime.kselect.enable=false). This was rolled out to 25% of traffic for dedicated pools and immediately reduced p99 to baseline for those instances.
- Medium-term patch: update kernel-selection heuristics to prefer the previous kv-merge path for contexts >1024 tokens or add a fast-path bypass when predicted KV size > X MB.
- Long-term: implement an asynchronous non-blocking kv-merge pipeline to avoid blocking token generation while merges are happening. Also add more robust telemetry around merge latencies to detect this earlier.

H100 throughput anomalies:
- Observed throughput drops for batched sampling on H100 after enabling the new kv-cache merge path in combination with the kselect optimizer. Theory: H100’s new SM scheduling + larger L2 interacts with our mempool alignment causing occasional warp-level serialization.
- Action: SRE (Priya) to spin a canary pool with the old mempool allocator and kselect enabled to see which component is the main contributor. Priya assigned (see action items).

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Avery / Samir: Draft revert plan and coordinate canary rollout to revert kernel-selection flag for all production H100 pools if further regressions occur (ETA: 2026-07-15 EOD).
- Lina: Prepare focused unit/regression tests for kv-cache merge path (add synthetic long-kv tests to harness-v5) and add tests to CI. (ETA: 2026-07-21)
- Elliot: Implement heuristic bypass (if KV_size > 64MB then fallback to legacy merge) and open PR for review. (PR target: 2026-07-20)
- Maya / QA (Jordan): Run extended soak for 48h on canary with kselect on + legacy mempool to validate throughput stability. Capture all telemetry. (Start: 2026-07-15)
- Priya (SRE): Create canary pool with old mempool allocator and provide perf metrics comparison dashboard; share link in channel. (ETA: 2026-07-15)
- Engineering docs: Add a short runbook entry for kernel-selection related regressions to Confluence (owner: Avery). (ETA: 2026-07-18)

Follow-ups / next meeting:
- Next sync planned: 2026-07-21 (weekly cadence) — focus will be: review fixes, CI regression coverage, extended soak results, and decide whether to re-enable kernel-select globally.
- Please add any additional data to the bench run spreadsheet and tag the PRs/JIRA tickets in the thread.

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Customer impact: No active customer incidents reported yet; internal alerts for p99 above 500ms triggered on some SLO dashboards for specific dedicated customers using long-context streaming. Customer Success was alerted and will be prepped to communicate if rollback affects planned improvements.
- Linked artifacts: see linked_artifacts field; PR #2481 is under review for the heuristic update (Elliot will link his follow-up PR when opened).

Raw logs / quick grep pointers (for engineers):
- grep pattern to find stalls: "cudaMemcpyAsync.*block.*kv_merge" in serving-runtime logs
- perf probe label: bench-kv-merge-2026-07-13
- Jenkins job: bench/nightly-serving-runtime-07-13 (console output contains per-run csvs)

End of notes.
